Data:Painting.annointing.json.Label: 'An Anointing'
Data:Painting.annointing.json.Desc: A silent crowd watches a robed priest bless a patient subject with sacred oils.

xexts.scrutiny: Signed 'CS'.

Data:Painting.behatted.json.Label: 'Portrait of a Behatted Lady'
Data:Painting.behatted.json.Desc: 'The More Prominent the Headgear, the Closer to the Glory'

xexts.scrutiny: The headgear is, without doubt, impressively prominent.

Data:Painting.birds.json.Label: 'Departure'
Data:Painting.birds.json.Desc: Here Valentine has painted gulls migrating across a darkening sea.

xexts.scrutiny: Each winter the black-backed gulls would leave Brancrug for warmer climes. Valentine would command a candle-lit dinner on the beach in their honour, with dancing and drumming, though he would never attend, only watch approvingly from the Gullscry Tower.

Data:Painting.bridge.ortucchio.json.Label: 'The Bridge at Ortucchio'
Data:Painting.bridge.ortucchio.json.Desc: A shadowy figure waits to accept its toll.

xexts.scrutiny: Signed 'Nina Lagasse'.

Data:Painting.chiliarch.victory.json.Label: The Chiliarch's Victory'
Data:Painting.chiliarch.victory.json.Desc: A blurred, menacing depiction of a vast, flabby carcass the colour of dirty sulphur, patched with brighter yellow. Signed 'Brulleau, 1861'.

xexts.scrutiny: The environment is a chilly desert beneath a low red sun. On closer inspection, the brighter patches seem to be golden blood, seeping from vast wounds.

Data:Painting.cockatoo.json.Label: 'Chac'
Data:Painting.cockatoo.json.Desc: Valentine Dewulf's magnificent green cockatoo. The painting is signed by Valentine himself.

xexts.scrutiny: Valentine, who had an interest in the religions of the new world, named his bird for the Mayan god of rain and thunder.

Data:Painting.coupleinthelibrary.json.Label: 'Love in a Quiet Place'
Data:Painting.coupleinthelibrary.json.Desc: One of Dr Levinsen's 'prefigures', a close (and impossible) copy of a painting made twenty years later by Kirchner, whose work Levinsen often anticipated in his mirror-dreams.

xexts.scrutiny: Levinsen has signed the painting but added 'E.L.K.?'

Data:Painting.donkey.json.Label: 'The Tattered Outlaw'
Data:Painting.donkey.json.Desc: Thirza Blake, Seventh Librarian of Hush House, liked painting donkeys. No-one else liked her donkey paintings, but Thirza never much cared what other people liked.

xexts.scrutiny: For some reason, this donkey has human eyes. There is also a cigarette-holder  - with no cigarette - sticking coyly out of the corner of its mouth.

Data:Painting.dontmesswithladyeva.json.Label: 'Eva and Abraham, 1724'
Data:Painting.dontmesswithladyeva.json.Desc: A magnificent depiction in oils of an elegantly dressed eighteenth century couple. The face of the gentleman, however, was long ago obliterated by a splash of some dark, corrosive substance.

xexts.scrutiny:
In her youth, Lady Eva is engaged to be married to an Abraham Wheelock of Monmouthshire, but in 1725 he leaves her at the altar. Furious and humiliated, she returns to Brancrug, and is not seen in London again.
Three days after her departure, Abraham Wheelock's body is washed up near Gravesend. His face is so badly pecked by birds that he is only identified by his belongings. These include a waxed pouch containing a letter addressed to Wheelock, whose contents seem to show he is a spy in the pay of the Austrians. Subsequent investigations suggest that the letter is a forgery, but the matter remains obscure.

Data:Painting.edge.json.Label: 'The First Threshold'
Data:Painting.edge.json.Desc: A horned double axe stands alone in a sandy desert.

xexts.scrutiny: Signed 'Nina Lagasse'.

Data:Painting.forge.json.Label: 'The First End'
Data:Painting.forge.json.Desc: A single candle burns against darkness; its flame is the crescent moon.

xexts.scrutiny: Signed 'Nina Lagasse'.

Data:Painting.grail.json.Label: 'The First Birth'
Data:Painting.grail.json.Desc: A single ripple disturbs the still surface of a well of blood.

xexts.scrutiny: Signed 'Nina Lagasse'.

Data:Painting.heart.json.Label: 'The Foundlings'
Data:Painting.heart.json.Desc: A pair of human eyes peer from darkness in a tangle of roots.

xexts.scrutiny: Signed 'Nina Lagasse'.

Data:Painting.julian.json.Label: 'Julian Coseley'
Data:Painting.julian.json.Desc: Julian is known to be Winter-long: at a prescribed date, his Hour-patron will ensure him a beautiful ending, but until then, he is even harder than most Long to dispose of finally. That said, he is known to have been defeated by an ascendant Long in the 1920s, and his true current status - a diminished survivor? a determined memory? something else? - is the subject of esoteric debate.

xexts.scrutiny: Coseley spent time at Hush House in the seventeenth century, but this painting, though undated, is clearly much more recent. It is also signed by Coseley himself. A gift to an imprisoned admirer?

Data:Painting.knock.json.Label: 'A Bargain'
Data:Painting.knock.json.Desc: A serpent laps at the blood that drips from a sewn-closed mouth.

xexts.scrutiny: Signed 'Nina Lagasse'.

Data:Painting.lantern.json.Label: 'Glory's Gift'
Data:Painting.lantern.json.Desc: A human figure is silhouetted against a blazing sun.

xexts.scrutiny: Signed 'Nina Lagasse'.

Data:Painting.mansus.json.Label: 'The Mansus'
Data:Painting.mansus.json.Desc: There have been many attempts to depict the House of the Sun. This, by the visionary painter known only as the Magyar, is the best known. It's signed and dated - if it's really the original, it must count as one of the great treasures of the House.

xexts.scrutiny: 'Beneath the skin of the world we find the Mansus, also called the World-Spine, also called the House of the Sun. The Mansus is the home of the Hours, on which the world depends, and a sojourning-place for certain departed souls. Above the House is the Glory, the origin of light, to which souls aspire. At the foot of the House, and around its walls - though it has no walls - is the Wood. Beneath the House is Nowhere…'

Data:Painting.mihail.altar.json.Label: Mihail in Glory
Data:Painting.mihail.altar.json.Desc: Mihail, Messenger to Darkness, depicted in the fullness of his power.

xexts.scrutiny: 'Mihail serves one who will profit by their endeavours.' [You were asked to place this on the Chancel altar behind the church.]

Data:Painting.mihail.sarcophagus.json.Label: Mihail in Chains
Data:Painting.mihail.sarcophagus.json.Desc: Mihail, Messenger to Darkness, depicted after his defeat.

xexts.scrutiny: 'Mihail serves one who carries fire in darkness.' [You were asked to place this in the Columbine Sarcophagus beneath the House.]

Data:Painting.moon.json.Label: 'The Wheel Still Turns'
Data:Painting.moon.json.Desc: A shining spoked Wheel with a vaguely organic look turns beneath a full moon that holds her finger to her lips.

xexts.scrutiny: Signed 'Nina Lagasse'.

Data:Painting.morgen.json.Label: 'Mlle Matutine'
Data:Painting.morgen.json.Desc: An alluring young woman with deep blue eyes hard and dark as sapphires.

xexts.scrutiny: Her teeth are very white; it is hard to be sure, but they seem also to be pointed…

Data:Painting.moth.json.Label: 'The First Answer'
Data:Painting.moth.json.Desc: A vast moth spirals towards a burning sun, alone in a star-speckled void.

xexts.scrutiny: Signed 'Nina Lagasse'.

Data:Painting.mountainlake.json.Label: 'To Hear Those Voices'
Data:Painting.mountainlake.json.Desc: A Levinsen 'prefigure' - a copy of a painting that would not be committed to canvas by the real artist for twenty years.

xexts.scrutiny: Kirchner, one of Levinsen's favourite pre-subjects. Kirchner and Levinsen fought in the Great War on opposite sides… but there is no reason to believe Kirchner had anything at all to do with Levinsen's death.

Data:Painting.munday.json.Label: 'Lord Munday'
Data:Painting.munday.json.Desc: A well-dressed, middle-aged gentleman with receding hair and a clear expression of astonished delight.

xexts.scrutiny: A small plaque reads MUNDAY ENDOWMENT - WITH GRATITUDE

Data:Painting.nectar.json.Label: 'Gods Return'
Data:Painting.nectar.json.Desc: A green shoot splits a rock.

xexts.scrutiny: Signed 'Nina Lagasse'.

Data:Painting.owl.json.Label: 'The Watcher'
Data:Painting.owl.json.Desc: Another of Valentine's paintings; a barn owl he nursed back to health.

xexts.scrutiny: Owls, of course, are associated with the Horned-Axe; but only one with one of her blades.

Data:Painting.picasso1.json.Label: 'Red, Blue'

xexts.scrutiny: Levinsen has signed it, but added a question mark after his signature.

Data:Painting.sacrifice.json.Label: 'A Sacrifice'

xexts.scrutiny: Signed 'CI'.

Data:Painting.scale.json.Label: 'The Hatching'
Data:Painting.scale.json.Desc: Human figures crawl from a clamshell.

xexts.scrutiny: Signed 'Nina Lagasse'.

Data:Painting.serena.json.Label: 'Dr Serena Blackwood'
Data:Painting.serena.json.Desc: No-one is in the picture - only an empty garden.

xexts.scrutiny: Blackwood abandoned Hush House for another library, the Invisible Serapeum in Alexandria. Is this a joke at her expense?

Data:Painting.sky.b.json.Label: 'As Above, So Below'
Data:Painting.sky.b.json.Desc: A framed page of illustrated vellum. Up close, the colours dazzle and puzzle.

xexts.scrutiny: A handwritten slip of paper reads ABBESS MELANCTHE, 1100? Melancthe's work was sometimes reckoned 'too radiant for the eye'…
